articles.title: El Ibiza vence y convence en Can Misses
articles.standfirst: El conjunto de Raúl Llona supera a un combativo Sant Andreu gracias a las paradas de Prieto y una segunda parte de alto nivel de Astals
articles.summary: El conjunto de Raúl Llona supera a un combativo Sant Andreu gracias a las paradas de Prieto y una segunda parte de alto nivel de Astals
articles.body: Can Misses vuelve a ser una fortaleza. La UD Ibiza cumplió con el guion de los grandes candidatos y derrotó por 2-0 a la UE Sant Andreu en la tercera jornada de la Primera Federación (Grupo 2), un triunfo construido con paciencia, un penalti bien resuelto en la primera media hora y una sentencia en el último suspiro. Con este resultado, los de Raúl Llona se instalan en la cuarta plaza con 6 puntos, mientras que el conjunto catalán, tras un arranque irregular, se queda en el vientre bajo de la tabla. FICHA TÉCNICA UD Ibiza: Prieto; Busto, Blasco, Curbelo, García; Varela (Almenara, 73’), Genrao, Ortiz (Astals, 46’), Valls (Fadel, 83’), Lazo (Justo, 61’) y Eslava (Yoldi, 61’). UE Sant Andreu: Juan; Méndez, Andreu, Blanco, Jiménez (Anaya, 74’); García (Torices, 46’), Pau Dabra (Alberto, 56’), Carrasco (Serrano, 79’), Bermejo (Armero, 56’); Delgado y Tovar. Goles: 1-0 Lazo(26′) de penalti, 2-0 Husto(90+1’) Árbitro: Álvaro Canovas García Villarrubiaasistido en bandas por Rita Cabañero Mompó y José Valerio Carrillo Moreno. 4º árbitro Hugo Alonso Martorell Tarjetas: amarillas a los locales Curbelo(61′), Almenara(74′) y Ángel Moreno (DE) (80′) y a los visitantes Pau Dabra(25′), Torices(67′) y Jordi(90′). Campo: Palladium Can Misses. Un penalti para romper el equilibrio. El choque tardó en abrirse. Fue en el minuto 26 cuando el Ibiza encontró la vía más rápida al gol: una pena máxima que los celestes transformaron para poner el 1-0 y encarrilar el partido antes del descanso, al que se llegó con esa mínima ventaja. Hasta ahí, el Sant Andreu había competido, aunque ya había pagado la primera factura disciplinaria con una amonestación en el minuto 22, síntoma de un encuentro trabado en el centro del campo. Tensión y cartulinas en la segunda mitad. El segundo acto se convirtió en una batalla de nervios. El árbitro repartió amarillas a ambos bandos —al Ibiza en los minutos 62 y 74, al Sant Andreu en el 68 y en el 90—, reflejo de un duelo áspero en el que el visitante buscó el empate sin terminar de encontrar el camino ante la meta defendida por Andrés Prieto. El guardameta local, uno de los hombres más veteranos del once, mantuvo su portería a cero por segunda vez en el arranque liguero, una constante que empieza a definir la identidad de este Ibiza. Golpe definitivo en el 90. Cuando el Sant Andreu volcaba sus fuerzas en busca de la igualada, el Ibiza aprovechó los espacios para firmar el 2-0 en el minuto 90, un gol de jugada que cerró el marcador y dejó sin margen de reacción a los de fuera. Fue la puntilla perfecta a un partido que el conjunto pitiuso gestionó con la madurez de quien sabe defender una renta. Los protagonistas del once local. Llona apostó por un dibujo de 4-5-1 con un bloque reconocible. En la medular convivieron nombres de peso como Pedro Ortiz y José Carlos Lazo, dos de los futbolistas de mayor valor de mercado de la plantilla, encargados de dar salida y control al balón. Atrás, la línea que formaron Pablo Busto, Jérémy Blasco, Eric Curbelo y Víctor García sostuvo el orden defensivo, con Genaro Rodríguez como recurso adicional. La referencia ofensiva recayó en Javier Eslava, con el peligroso Manu Justo —máximo valor de mercado del banquillo local— esperando su oportunidad entre los suplentes. El Sant Andreu, sin pegada. El equipo dirigido desde el banquillo visitante saltó con un 4-4-2 comandado por su capitán Jordi Méndez en defensa y con el arquero Ramón Juan bajo palos. Arriba, la pareja formada por Jaume Tovar y Álex Bermejo Escribano no logró inquietar de forma decisiva a la zaga celeste, y ni siquiera la entrada de recambios como el joven Pablo Agudín —el futbolista de mayor tasación de la expedición catalana— o el internacional puertorriqueño Jeremy de León bastó para cambiar la dinámica. El Sant Andreu suma así su segunda derrota en tres jornadas y se mantiene con 3 puntos, decimotercero, en zona de aguas revueltas. La lectura clasificatoria. El Grupo 2 vive un arranque apretadísimo en su cabeza: Gimnàstic de Tarragona y Real Jaén comparten liderato con 7 puntos, seguidos muy de cerca por Real Murcia (6), la propia UD Ibiza (6) y el Villarreal B (6). La victoria permite a los pitiusos mantenerse pegados a los puestos de privilegio y responder a la única mancha de su casillero, esa derrota que les impide compartir el techo del grupo. Con 6 goles a favor y 4 en contra, el Ibiza exhibe una producción ofensiva pareja a la de los primeros, aunque con margen de mejora en la solidez. Un rival que debe reaccionar. Para el Sant Andreu, el escenario es más delicado. Con una sola victoria en tres salidas y a las puertas de la zona baja, el conjunto catalán necesita empezar a sumar de tres para no descolgarse. Su producción goleadora —apenas 2 tantos en tres partidos— es la asignatura pendiente más evidente de un equipo que, sin embargo, ha mostrado capacidad de competir en la primera parte de este mismo duelo. El detalle. El 2-0 no admite discusión en el marcador, pero el partido tuvo el matiz de los encuentros que se deciden por eficacia más que por dominio abrumador. El Ibiza acertó cuando tuvo que acertar —desde los once metros y en el momento de rematar la faena— y cerró filas cuando el rival apretó. Es la receta de los equipos con aspiraciones, y Can Misses volvió a ser un fortín que empieza a pesar en las cuentas del Grupo 2. Lo que viene. El calendario no da tregua en una categoría tan igualada, donde cada jornada reordena la parte alta. El Ibiza tratará de encadenar victorias para escalar hasta el liderato, mientras que el Sant Andreu buscará en su próximo compromiso el triunfo que le devuelva la confianza y le aleje de la zona de peligro. En una Primera Federación donde los márgenes son mínimos, sumar de tres como local es, muchas veces, la diferencia entre soñar y sufrir.

articles.title: 'I hope they don’t go to prayer later': Furious Ruben Neves hits back after Al-Taawoun fans taunt him with Diogo Jota’s name
articles.summary: Football News: Ruben Neves expresses anger at Al-Taawoun fans who taunted him by chanting the name of his late friend Diogo Jota during a match. The Portuguese midfielder's emotional response highlights the deep bond he shared with Jota and the pain caused by the incident.
articles.body: Ruben Neves had little to complain about on the pitch as Al-Hilal stormed to a 6-0 victory, but the Portugal international was visibly angered by what happened in the stands.Neves was targeted by Al-Taawoun supporters during Saturday's meeting in Buraidah, with fans chanting the name of his late friend and former Portugal team-mate Diogo Jota. The incident left the Al-Hilal midfielder furious, and he had a pointed response when he was approached after the final whistle.Neves reacts after Al-Taawoun fans chant Jota's nameAl-Hilal produced a dominant display in the seventh round of the Saudi Roshn League, sweeping aside Al-Taawoun 6-0 at the hosts' stadium.Yet the result was overshadowed for Neves by an incident involving a group of Al-Taawoun supporters.A video shared on X by Aziz Al-Dahmashi appeared to show an altercation between Neves and fans during the match. The trouble flared after supporters began chanting Jota's name, which appeared to provoke an angry response from the Portuguese midfielder.Neves was seen pointing towards the sky and telling the supporters: “God sees you.”When he later walked past the media after the match, he did not go into detail about the incident or single out any individual. Instead, he offered a brief response that made his feelings clear.“I hope they don't go to prayer later after what they did,” Neves said.His remark appeared to be a direct condemnation of the use of Jota's name during the match, contrasting the behaviour he had witnessed with religious and human values.Neves chose not to elaborate further, allowing those few words to speak for themselves.Neves shared a deep bond with Liverpool icon Diogo JotaThe significance of the incident lies in the relationship Neves had with Jota, who died alongside his younger brother André Silva, a professional footballer who played for Penafiel in Portugal’s second division, in a tragic car accident in the Spanish region of Cernadilla in July last year.Their friendship began at Porto, where both players came through the club's system before continuing their careers together at Wolverhampton Wanderers. They later shared the Portugal dressing room, remaining close as their careers developed at the highest level.Jota went on to become a hugely important figure for Liverpool after joining the club in 2020. His movement, pressing and instinctive finishing made him a key part of Jurgen Klopp's attack, while his ability to score from difficult positions quickly made him a favourite at Anfield.He scored decisive goals in the Premier League and Champions League, helped Liverpool compete for major honours and became known for his intelligence inside the penalty area. Jota was not simply a squad player during his time on Merseyside; he was a forward trusted in the biggest matches and a player whose goals regularly changed the course of games.His importance to Liverpool was reflected in the affection shown by supporters, team-mates and staff following his death. Tributes poured in from across the football world, with the club and its fans mourning a player remembered not only for his performances but also for his character away from the pitch.Neves has spoken publicly on more than one occasion about the profound grief he experienced following Jota's death. Their connection had been built over many years, through club football, international duty and a friendship that continued long after they stopped playing for the same team.That history made the chanting particularly painful for Neves, who appeared to view the use of Jota's name as a deeply personal provocation rather than ordinary football banter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mikel Arteta rages at Sunderland penalty decision after Arsenal win at Stadium of Light: 'This cannot happen'
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta was left furious by the award of Sunderland's penalty during Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light, saying such decisions can cost a side a Premier League title; David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's spot kick as Gunners claimed a fourth straight win
articles.body:
The home side were awarded a spot kick in the 54th minute when defender Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have held Sunderland's Dan Ballard by referee John Brooks.

"The referee's call of penalty to Sunderland for a holding offence by Konsa on Ballard was checked and confirmed by VAR," said a statement published by the Premier League Match Centre.

The statement continued by quoting the interaction between on-pitch referee Brooks and the VAR.

As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights

Latest news and rumours: Sunderland | Arsenal

"REF: 'He's all over him at the near post facing the wrong way.' VAR: 'I'm happy that it's a holding offence. The foul is confirmed. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty.'"

David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's spot kick and Bruno Guimaraes scored Arsenal's opening goal just 121 seconds later but Arteta vented his anger at the decision despite the result.

"The first question we have to discuss is this," he said at the start of his press conference. "This is not acceptable at this level.

"It was a beautiful game of football with two teams, with an atmosphere in the stadium that was unbelievable.

"Sunderland are so well organised, they are so good in so many phases, they have great players and they create a lot of issues. We have to cope with all of that in a really difficult week.

"And on top of that, we have to go through what we have done today, that, in my opinion, is not acceptable.

"I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation, or the way the VAR has to intervene.

"I'm sad that we have to discuss this after such a beautiful game, that at this level, has the gravity of that. Because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship.

"At this level, with all the work we put in, this cannot happen."

Arsenal's victory was wrapped up by a late Bukayo Saka penalty but Arteta, who was booked for going out of his technical area earlier in the game, was similarly angry in his post-match interview with TNT Sports , describing the incident as a "judo roll".

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any context, in any league," he added.

articles.title: Siverio relanza al Jaén en este inicio de temporada
articles.standfirst: El delantero firmó el tanto del triunfo lagarto que permitió a los blancos encadenar su segunda victoria del curso a domicilio
articles.summary: El delantero firmó el tanto del triunfo lagarto que permitió a los blancos encadenar su segunda victoria del curso a domicilio
articles.body: El Real Jaén se marchó de tierras turolenses con un botín de oro. Un solitario tanto de Marco Siverio Toro en el minuto 63 bastó para que el conjunto andaluz sumara su segunda victoria del curso y se instalara en la zona alta del Grupo 2 de la Primera Federación, mientras el CD Teruel prolongó un arranque de temporada preocupante: tres jornadas, un solo punto y, lo más alarmante, cero goles a favor. FICHA TÉCNICA Teruel: Zarco; Borge (Nathan, 64'), Álvaro López, Relu (Borikó, 78'), Joserra; Edu Gallardo, Romera (Hugo Redón, 70'), Albisua, Mario Sesé (Belevonis, 78'); Moraitis (Lluís Llácer, 64'), Sergio Moreno. Real Jaén: Morillas; Moha, José Álvarez, Álex Pérez, David Serrano; Caballero, Adri (Montejano, 57'); Chino (Peque Polo, 83'), Castillo (Busi, 57'), Mario Martos (Fran Gallego, 83'); Marco Siverio. Gol: 0-1 (63') Siverio. Árbitro: Rodríguez Recio (Madrid). Amonestó a Relu (4'), Moha (12'), Adri (33'), Caballero (51') y Busi (87'). Incidencias: Pinilla. El desenlace de un duelo de tensión contenida El choque, disputado el sábado 12 de septiembre a las 18:45, correspondiente a la tercera jornada, fue un pulso áspero más que un festival ofensivo. El acta lo refleja con nitidez: cuatro amonestaciones antes del descanso —Relu por parte local en el minuto 4, y Moha Sanhaji (12'), Adri (33') y, ya en la reanudación, Antonio Caballero (51') en las filas visitantes— dibujaron un partido de mucha fricción y pocos espacios. Con el 0-0 al descanso, el técnico del Jaén movió ficha pronto. En el minuto 57 introdujo a David Gómez Montejano y a Dani Rodríguez por Adri y Nacho Castillo, un doble cambio que reoxigenó al equipo. Apenas seis minutos después llegó la recompensa: en el 63, Marco Siverio Toro firmó el único gol del encuentro para poner el 0-1 que ya no se movería. El gol obligó a reaccionar al Teruel, que respondió con un aluvión de cambios. En el 64, entraron Lluís Llácer y Nathaniel Nicholas por Andrés Borge Martín y Panagiotis Moraitis; en el 70, Hugo Redón por Miguel Romera; y en el 79, la doble variación de Santi Borikó y Christos Belevonis por Relu y Mario Sesé. El banquillo local vació el cargador buscando un empate que nunca apareció. El Jaén, por su parte, gestionó la ventaja con oficio, refrescando piernas con Francisco Gallego y Peque Polo (83') para amarrar los tres puntos. Un héroe con experiencia El nombre del partido es el de Marco Siverio Toro. El delantero, titular con el dorsal 9, resolvió el único momento en que el marcador se rompió y decidió una tarde de trincheras. Su acierto en la finalización marcó la diferencia entre dos equipos que, sobre el papel, habían firmado un igualado 0-0 durante más de una hora. Detrás, la solidez defensiva del Real Jaén volvió a ser su gran argumento. El bloque dispuesto en 3-5-2, con Jaime Morillas bajo palos y una línea de tres centrales encabezada por David Serrano y Alejandro Pérez, mantuvo la portería a cero por segunda vez en tres jornadas. No es casualidad que el conjunto jienense presuma de la mejor defensa compartida del grupo. Lo que dice la clasificación El triunfo tiene una traducción inmediata y muy dulce en la tabla del Grupo 2. El Real Jaén alcanza los 7 puntos (dos victorias y un empate, sin derrotas) y se sitúa en la segunda posición, empatado a puntos con el líder, el Gimnàstic de Tarragona, y con idéntico balance goleador: 6 goles a favor y solo 2 en contra. Ambos comparten un diferencial de +4 que subraya la fortaleza del inicio andaluz. El Jaén se ha metido de lleno en la pelea por las plazas nobles y confirma que su candidatura al ascenso va en serio. En el otro vestuario, el panorama es sombrío. El CD Teruel se descuelga hasta el decimonoveno puesto con un único punto en tres partidos (un empate y dos derrotas). El dato más elocuente es su casillero de goles: 0 a favor y 5 en contra, el peor ataque del grupo. El equipo turolense no ha sido capaz de perforar ninguna portería en lo que va de campeonato, y esa sequía lo tiene ya coqueteando con los puestos de descenso, apenas por delante del colista Algeciras CF, todavía sin puntuar. La lucha por no hundirse La zona baja del Grupo 2 empieza a tomar forma temprano. Por debajo del Teruel solo aparece el Algeciras CF (0 puntos), mientras justo por encima se agolpan el CE Europa (1 punto, -4) y varios equipos con 3 puntos como Hércules CF, Real Zaragoza o UE Sant Andreu. Para el Teruel, la urgencia es doble: necesita puntos, sí, pero sobre todo necesita empezar a marcar. Sin gol, cualquier plan de rescate se queda a medias. Jugadores a seguir - Marco Siverio Toro (Real Jaén): el ariete que ya sabe lo que es decidir partidos en esta categoría. Su gol de la jornada lo convierte en la referencia ofensiva del líder colista de la clasificación por diferencia de goles. - Panagiotis Moraitis (CD Teruel): el delantero griego, el futbolista de mayor valor de mercado del once local, es la esperanza de un ataque que necesita despertar cuanto antes. Su relevo en el minuto 64 refleja la búsqueda desesperada de soluciones del banquillo turolense. - David Serrano (Real Jaén): central fiable en el 3-5-2 andaluz, pieza de una zaga que suma su segunda portería a cero y sostiene el gran arranque del equipo. Conclusión El Real Jaén se marchó de Teruel con la sensación del trabajo bien hecho: un gol, una portería a cero y siete puntos que lo colocan hombro con hombro con el Gimnàstic en lo más alto del Grupo 2. El CD Teruel, en cambio, afronta una encrucijada temprana. Con cero goles en tres jornadas y colgando de la penúltima plaza, el reto ya no es solo sumar, sino recuperar la fe en un ataque que, por ahora, no encuentra el camino a la portería rival.

articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado vs. Weber State Box Score, Julian Lewis and Top Player Stats, Highlights
articles.summary: The Colorado Buffaloes' home opener came in style with a 52-21 victory over Weber State as Deion Sanders and the team moved to 2-0 to kick off the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Colorado Buffaloes' home opener came in style with a 52-21 victory over Weber State as Deion Sanders and the team moved to 2-0 to kick off the 2026 season.

Colorado was a massive 34.5-point favorite over Weber State on Saturday, per Fanduel Sportsbook , living up to the hype behind a standout performance from sophomore quarterback Julian Lewis.

Hot off an exhilarating Week 1, one-point win over Georgia Tech thanks to a blocked field goal as the clock expired, the Buffs opened the season 2-0 for the first time since 2023.

Lewis threw for 124 yards on 14-of-27 attempts with one touchdown in the season opener.

Turning around in Week 2 against a 1-1 Weber State team, Colorado put 10 toes to the ground and dominated the Big Sky school behind a standout performance from its sophomore quarterback.

Lewis threw three touchdown passes in the first quarter, connecting with DeAndre Moore Jr. for 66 yards, Joseph Williams for 63 yards and Ernest Campbell for 48 yards. Lewis did fumble on a sack, but his impressive offensive performance overshadowed the mistake in the first quarter.

Adding to his impressive first half, Lewis rushed for a touchdown and connected with Williams again for another score, while running back Micah Welch ran one in as the Buffs took a commanding 42-14 lead into the break.

Lewis entered halftime with 331 yards on an 83 percent completion rate, four passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown.

Lewis led the team out of halftime, powering the offense down the field to set up Elliot Arnold for a 52-yard field goal and add three quick points.

With a 31-point lead secured, Lewis was sent to the bench to watch his team finish out the victory.

The undefeated start is an encouraging sign of a potential turnaround year for Sanders, who led the Buffaloes to a 2024 bowl game against the BYU Cougars but struggled last season, finishing with just three wins.

Colorado will look to keep the streak going as they hit the road to play the Northwestern Wildcats next Saturday.

articles.title: El Cartagena se quedó corto en el Cerro del Espino
articles.standfirst: Se adelantó gracias a Dacosta y luego encajó antes del descanso
articles.summary: Se adelantó gracias a Dacosta y luego encajó antes del descanso
articles.body: El Rayo Majadahonda y el FC Cartagena repartieron puntos (1-1) en la tercera jornada del Grupo 2 de la Primera Federación, en un duelo que dejó a los dos equipos con sensaciones opuestas pese al mismo resultado: el conjunto madrileño respiró para cortar una racha negativa, mientras que el cuadro cartagenerista mantuvo su condición de invicto pero cedió puntos por segunda vez en tres partidos. El encuentro, disputado el sábado 12 de septiembre a las 21:00, se decidió en un tramo caliente de la primera mitad, con dos goles en apenas siete minutos que marcaron el guion de la noche. FICHA TÉCNICA Rayo Majadahonda, 1: Miguel Prieto; Ale Díez, Sina, Amaro (Daniel Ramos, min.71), Óscar Mesa; Tarsi Aguado, Quintanilla (Pozo, min.93), Yoshimura, Jeremy (Raúl Hernández, min.93); Cambra (Celorio, min.71) y Manín. Fútbol Club Cartagena, 1: Lucho García; Dani Perejón, Imanol Baz, Luca Lohr, Nacho Martínez; Clavería (Jean Jules, min.68), De Blasis, Álex Guti (Javi Ajenjo, min.68), Dacosta (Benito Ramírez, min.89); Marcos Moreno (Abde Lah, min.89) e Iban Ribeiro. Goles: 0-1, min.33: Dacosta. 1-1,min.40: Manín. Árbitro: Alfredo Ramo Andrés, del comité aragonés. Mostró la tarjeta amarilla a los locales Jeremy (min.4), Tarsi Aguado (min.28) y Celorio (min.93). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la Liga en el grupo 2 de la Primera RFEF de fútbol que se disputó en el estadio del Cerro del Espino ante unos 2.000 espectadores, 200 de ellos desplazados desde Cartagena. Un primer tiempo que lo decidió todo El Cartagena golpeó primero. En el minuto 32, Raúl Dacosta culminó una acción bien trenzada para batir a Miguel Prieto y adelantar a los visitantes. El tanto llevó la firma de Nacho Martínez en la asistencia, el veterano lateral que puso el balón para que Dacosta abriera el marcador y silenciara al ambiente local. La reacción del Rayo Majadahonda, sin embargo, fue inmediata. Apenas siete minutos después, en el 39, Manin Gonzaga igualó la contienda para poner el 1-1 con el que se llegaría al descanso. El delantero, que ya venía siendo una referencia arriba para los de Majadahonda, aprovechó su ocasión para devolver la igualdad a un choque que hasta entonces se le había puesto cuesta arriba a los suyos. Antes de los goles, el partido ya había mostrado su carácter bronco: Jeremy Jorge vio la primera amarilla local en el minuto 4, y Tarsi Aguado fue amonestado en el 28, síntomas de la tensión con la que ambos equipos afrontaron los primeros compases. Una segunda parte de ajustes y sin premio Tras el intermedio, el marcador se congeló. El Cartagena movió el banquillo pronto: en el minuto 68, el técnico visitante dio entrada a Jean Jules Mvondo y a Javier Ajenjo Hyjek por Pablo Clavería y Álex Guti, buscando frescura en la medular. El Rayo respondió con sus propios cambios en el 71, con Daniel Ramos por Antonio Amaro y Neco Celorio —por lesión— sustituyendo a José Cambra. El tramo final trajo más rotaciones que ocasiones claras. El Cartagena dio minutos a Benito Ramírez y a Abdel Lah Mohamed en los minutos 88 y 89, mientras el Rayo agotaba su cupo en el 90 con David Del Pozo y Raúl Hernández. En ese mismo minuto, Neco Celorio recibió una tarjeta amarilla, cerrando el capítulo disciplinario de una noche intensa que acabó como había quedado tras el primer tiempo: con tablas. Lo que dice la clasificación El reparto de puntos mantiene al FC Cartagena en la sexta posición del Grupo 2 con 5 puntos, fruto de un balance de un triunfo y dos empates en tres jornadas, todavía sin conocer la derrota (4 goles a favor, 2 en contra). Es un arranque sólido, aunque los dos empates dejan la sensación de que el equipo ha dejado escapar la oportunidad de instalarse en la zona alta, encabezada por el Gimnàstic de Tarragona y el Real Jaén, ambos con 7 puntos. Para el Rayo Majadahonda, el punto sabe a poco en lo clasificatorio pero puede valer mucho en lo anímico. Los madrileños son decimosextos con un solo punto, tras un balance de tres empates... no: un empate y dos derrotas en tres partidos, con 3 goles marcados y 5 encajados. El equipo aún no ha ganado esta temporada y se mueve en la parte baja de la tabla, a un paso de los puestos más comprometidos que ocupan Juventud Torremolinos, CE Europa, CD Teruel y un Algeciras CF que sigue sin puntuar. Los protagonistas En el bando visitante, la pareja Nacho Martínez–Raúl Dacosta fue la que decidió la aportación ofensiva del Cartagena. Dacosta, autor del gol, se retiró en el minuto 88 tras cumplir con su cometido, mientras que la experiencia de Nacho Martínez volvió a resultar determinante desde la banda. En el Rayo Majadahonda, Manin Gonzaga se erige como el hombre a seguir. Su gol no solo rescató un empate, sino que subrayó su papel como principal amenaza ofensiva de un equipo que necesita urgentemente convertir el buen pie de su delantero en victorias. Conclusión Un 1-1 que refleja el equilibrio de un partido resuelto en siete minutos de la primera parte. El Cartagena preserva su invicto pero se aleja levemente del grupo de cabeza; el Rayo Majadahonda suma su primer punto lejos de la derrota y se agarra a la reacción de Gonzaga como punto de partida para enderezar un inicio de temporada complicado. Para ambos, el mensaje es claro: hay margen de mejora, y las próximas jornadas dirán si este empate fue un peldaño o una oportunidad perdida.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Not 'Satisfied' With Colorado's 52 Points But Hypes Julian Lewis' Historic Performance
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders was not satisfied with his team's home opener despite quarterback Julian Lewis making program history in a blowout win over Weber State.
articles.body:
Colorado coach Deion Sanders was not satisfied with his team's home opener despite quarterback Julian Lewis making program history in a blowout win over Weber State.

Lewis scored five touchdowns in the first half, but the Buffaloes were held to 10 points in the final two quarters of a 52-21 win over Weber State.

"We didn't capitalize on offense. We only scored 52 points... There's no way we are satisfied with the outcome," Sanders said after the win, per Oliver Hayes of the Buff Stampede.

Sanders added he felt his team letting up on offense was due to a "lack of not being there before," per Hayes .

The Colorado coach also said he was happy with the performance from Lewis, who set a program record with four first-half passing touchdowns, according to Hayes .

Lewis shared a similar message to Sanders' in his own postgame availability.

"We're definitely still not where we want to be... there's time to grow, and there's room to grow, but we're ready, and I think everybody is on the same page with that," Lewis said Saturday (h/t DNVR Buffs). "Nobody is satisfied with where we're at."

Lewis became the first quarterback in program history to throw four touchdown passes in an opening half during the Buffaloes' 52-21 win.

The 18-year-old finished the game as the first Colorado quarterback since Shedeur Sanders to put up at least 350 passing yards and four touchdowns without an interception, per ESPN Insights .

Colorado's defense and special teams didn't have nearly as successful of a night.

The Buffaloes allowed three touchdowns and gave up 372 total yards to their FCS opponents. Colorado's special teams were flagged for multiple penalties after previously struggling in the team's Week 1 win over Georgia Tech.

Sanders said ahead of Saturday's game he was "not concerned" about his special teams because in part because he planned to change up his personnel. There could be more changes coming as the Buffaloes look to make more improvements before returning to action next Saturday at Northwestern.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 2
articles.summary: Welcome back, chaos. We're glad you're here.
articles.body:
Welcome back, chaos. We're glad you're here.

Oklahoma State kicked off Week 2 in style, taking down No. 6 Oregon and providing the first shocking upset of the 2026 season. Also in the early window, Michigan bounced back from a horrible day to topple 11th-ranked Oklahoma.

As it turns out, that madness was merely the appetizer to a downright stunner in the featured game of Saturday's slate.

Texas fell behind top-ranked Ohio State in a hurry, but a furious fourth-quarter surge propelled the Longhorns to an incredible 24-23 victory. That comeback highlighted a fascinating day around college football.

This piece was updated throughout Saturday's action.

Western Michigan is a quality Group of Six team. It's important to remember that context when discussing Michigan's performance in Week 1.

At the same time, it was wholly embarrassing for the Wolverines to play so poorly. The offense looked horrible, and only a controversial replay decision gave U-M an opportunity to complete a miracle Hail Mary.

Given that performance, of course U-M was an underdog in Week 2. Oklahoma shut down Michigan's offense in last season's meeting, too.

So, naturally, the Wolverines knocked off OU 17-10.

Michigan still struggled to move the ball, gaining just 263 yards and scoring its winning touchdown after Jyaire Hill returned an interception to the six-yard line. This defense continues to carry the Maize and Blue.

But after such a terrible Week 1 showing, that's a massive win for Michigan.

Last season, Oregon laid a 69-3 smackdown on Oklahoma State while racking up 631 yards of offense and ceding only 211. About two weeks later, OSU fired longtime head coach Mike Gundy.

Oklahoma State—which was a 24-point underdog—stunned Oregon 39-31 this time around. Drew Mestemaker threw for 317 yards, rushed for 109 and totaled three touchdowns, including a gutsy rushing score in which he leapt over one Oregon defender and took a monster hit from another while airborne.

Incredibly, the Pokes became the first team in FBS history to snap a 10-plus game losing streak by beating a top-10 opponent.

Much of the national conversation will focus on how Oregon's rest-of-season outlook has changed, but Oklahoma State fully deserves its crown today.

How does Michigan, on the heels of nearly falling to a MAC team, outlast a borderline top-10 SEC team? How does Oklahoma State, following a 14-point loss at Tulsa, turn around and defeat a perceived national championship threat?

For good measure, how does Utah State fall to lower-division Idaho State last Saturday yet take No. 19 Washington to the brink in a 16-14 U-Dub win?

As a card-carrying member of Team Chaos, I love that college football does not make sense. Upsets fuel an essential part of the sport.

How in the world, though, are we supposed to predict that? You want educated analysis, and I—along with hundreds, thousands of others—spend a large number of hours watching, dissecting, reviewing and explaining these games.

But sometimes, this beautiful sport just doesn't make sense . It's the best.

When the final score is an 87-3 blowout—and that's not a typo—you're bound to see an impressive stat line or two. Generally, those players merit a golf clap while acknowledging the enormous gap in competition level.

However, we need to talk about Michael Scott's Dundie-worthy performance in James Madison's rout of FCS program Wagner.

A sophomore wideout, Scott made three catches for 45 yards. Oh, and he returned two punts for touchdowns—a couple of fun runs, you could say—and nearly took a kickoff to the house, returning it 92 yards before getting pushed out of bounds.

It's only Week 2. Because there aren't a ton of return touchdowns in a given season, though, Scott has legitimately put himself on the All-American radar.

That's a very quiet, very important takeaway from an otherwise forgettable game.

Michigan won! That was neat for the Big Ten.

Even beyond Oregon's jaw-dropping loss to Oklahoma State, though, the conference had a rather mediocre set of games in the daylight.

Washington needed to defend a Hail Mary as time expired to clip Utah State, escaping with a 16-14 victory. Minnesota had no answers for Kamario Taylor as visiting Mississippi State rolled to a 38-13 rout.

Purdue dropped a dramatic 38-36 double-overtime game at home to Wake Forest, and Illinois walked off its field with a 31-27 loss to Duke.

Safe to say the Big Ten would like Ohio State to salvage the evening slate!

BYU entered the campaign as a front-runner in the Big 12, but opening its conference slate with Arizona was no gift. Last year, it took a couple of overtimes for BYU to emerge with a nerve-wracking win.

Fortunately for the Cougars, they finished off the Cats more comfortably this season. Bear Bachmeier totaled 254 yards and four touchdowns in a 28-17 triumph.

The outcome wasn't a surprise, given 15th-ranked BYU's status as the favorite. The result doesn't alter the Big 12 discussion, either—but that's exactly the point. BYU prevented Arizona from throwing an early wrench into the league race.

For the Cougs, maintaining the status quo was the goal. Mission accomplished.

When the College Football Playoff rankings are unveiled, updated and eventually finalized, will Memphis be ruing this moment?

Perhaps a few losses are on the horizon for the Tigers. Two or three months from today, one setback in mid-September might not be the important storyline. Maybe they'll have an 8-4 record anyway.

Or, well, this could be a decisive factor for the CFP selection committee.

Memphis began the campaign with a win at UNLV—a presumed front-runner in the Mountain West—and traveled to Boise State in Week 2. Win on the blue turf, and the Tigers would be the most impressive Group of Six team early on. Remember, the highest-ranked G6 program will be included in the Playoff.

After halftime, though, Memphis saw a 20-17 lead become a 24-20 deficit. Boise soon pulled ahead 31-20 and ultimately won 38-20.

Memphis is not finished. There's time to recover.

But that was a big opportunity squandered in one disappointing half.

Through 30 minutes, the story had a completely different tone.

On the opening snap of the clash with top-ranked Ohio State, Texas lost a fumble. On the Longhorns' second drive, a potential 50-yard completion from Arch Manning to Cam Coleman turned into a freaky interception.

Fast-forward to halftime, and Texas trailed 20-3 as a stunned crowd wondered if the school could metaphorically fire Steve Sarkisian into the sun.

Again. Ohio State was going to beat the Horns again . It happened in the CFP two years ago, then to kick off the 2025 campaign as well.

Somehow, the story changed in the fourth quarter.

Manning hit Ryan Wingo for a short touchdown. The defense forced a three-and-out before Hollywood Smothers ran in a score. Ohio State's miserable missed-clutch-field-goal problem made another untimely appearance, and Texas bullied its way down the field for a last-minute touchdown from Smothers and a 24-23 win.

Texas has a brutal schedule ahead, but the Longhorns locked up a tremendous victory for their résumé.

The opening half seemed like a masterclass. Ohio State dominated every phase of the game, building a commanding 17-point advantage at the break.

Jeremiah Smith was the best player on the field, shredding the Texas secondary with accurate passes from Julian Sayin. The defense pounced on a fumble, lucked into an interception and brilliantly forced a turnover on downs.

Everything was going right—until it all went horribly wrong.

You could point to conservative play-calling, yet another key opportunity wasted on special teams or a defense that couldn't handle Texas' physicality down the stretch. So many issues combined at the worst moment for OSU, and the Buckeyes blew a 17-point halftime lead for the first time in program history.

Day is 80-13 as Ohio State's full-time coach. He's taken the Bucks to the Playoff five times and won a national championship in 2024.

But his approval rating, after this disaster, will be sinking to an all-time low.

Between the returning players from a Big 12-winning team and an experienced group of transfers, Texas Tech opened 2026 as the obvious league favorite.

The good news is the Red Raiders are 2-0.

The bad news is they haven't been convincing in either win.

Last week, Texas Tech struggled to finish drives against FCS team Abilene Christian and meandered to a 33-10 victory. Saturday, the Red Raiders trailed Oregon State in the fourth quarter. They ended up with a 35-24 margin, but a garbage-time touchdown makes it appear more comfortable than it was.

Hey, wins are wins. While aesthetics matter, results are most important.

Texas Tech, however, is poised for a major jump in competition as 22nd-ranked Houston comes to town for a Friday night showdown in Week 3. It'll be a pivotal moment for the Red Raiders' perception this season.

articles.title: College football Week 2 winners and losers: No. 6 Oregon's upset loss to Oklahoma State is bad, but doesn't immediately end Ducks' playoff hopes
articles.summary: Oregon was a 24-point favorite at kickoff. In 2024, Notre Dame made the CFP despite a Week 2 loss to Northern Illinois as a 28.5-point favorite.
articles.body:
No. 6 Oregon could find itself outside the AP Top 25 on Sunday after a shocking upset loss at Oklahoma State on Saturday.

But the Ducks' College Football Playoff hopes are far from over, even if their margin for error is a whole lot slimmer after Oklahoma State's 39-31 win as a 24-point underdog.

After a Week 1 win over Boise State that was far from pristine, Oregon was sloppier and even more undisciplined against the Cowboys. Yes, the defense got a pick 6 and set up another touchdown with an interception, but if both of those deflected passes fall harmlessly to the turf, the Ducks wouldn't have been in a position to force overtime with two minutes to go.

But in an incredibly fitting finish for Oregon's offense, Dierre Hill Jr. dropped a simple toss from QB Dante Moore and Oklahoma State made a game-sealing fumble recovery.

An Oregon offense that features the potential No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft in Moore had just 50 total yards at halftime, went just 5-of-14 on third downs and failed on all three of its fourth-down attempts.

With just under seven minutes to go and Oklahoma State up five, Oregon needed 8 yards for a first down at its own 33-yard line. Coach Dan Lanning left the offense on the field. Moore's pass fell incomplete.

Minutes later, Oklahoma State was up eight.

Was Lanning unable to trust his defense? Oklahoma State averaged nearly 6.7 yards a play and ran 83 plays on a 95-degree day in Stillwater. A week ago, Oklahoma State averaged 4.3 yards per play and scored 10 points in a 14-point loss to Tulsa.

Even if you believe Oklahoma State is much improved thanks to new coach Eric Morris, QB Drew Mestemaker, RB Caleb Hawkins and a host of other transfers from North Texas and other schools, it was an embarrassing loss for the Ducks. In Week 2 of the 2025 season, Oregon pasted Oklahoma State 69-3 in a sure sign that Mike Gundy's time at Oklahoma State was quickly approaching its expiration date.

You don't find many 74-point swings from year to year in college football.

Yet for how bad Saturday's defeat is, we already have multiple examples through the first two years of the 12-team College Football Playoff of heavy favorites losing outright and still making the postseason field. If Oregon corrects its numerous mistakes from the first two weeks — and that's admittedly no guarantee — the loss can be overcome.

Through the first two seasons of the expanded playoff, four teams have made the CFP after losing as at least a two-touchdown favorite. And the teams on the wrong end of the two biggest upsets met for the national championship in January of 2025.

In Week 2 of the 2024 season, Northern Illinois pulled off one of the biggest upsets in modern college football with a 16-14 win over Notre Dame as a 28.5-point underdog. Notre Dame's offense was horrific in the loss. But the Irish found their footing, won their last 10 regular season games and then won three playoff games before losing to Ohio State.

The Buckeyes' embarrassment came a bit later in the season, and Ohio State fans would appreciate not being reminded of it. OSU ended the regular season with a 13-10 loss to Michigan as a 19.5-point favorite . But despite starting the playoff as the No. 8 seed, Ohio State went on a tear in the playoff that included a Rose Bowl blowout of Oregon to win its first national title in 10 seasons.

That Ohio State team isn't too dissimilar from Oregon, as players like Denzel Burke , Emeka Egbuka , TreVeyon Henderson and Tyleik Williams returned for another season instead of going pro in 2024. Along with Moore, Oregon retained DE Matayo Uiagalelei, DL Bear Alexander , TE Jamari Johnson and others in its pursuit of the national title.

Will it work out for Oregon like it did Ohio State? The odds are still stacked against the Ducks. But they also aren't zero.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers:

Duke: The Blue Devils won the ACC a season ago and have already beaten two teams they lost to in 2025. Duke started last season 1-2 thanks to losses to Illinois and Tulane. A week ago, Duke's defense dominated in a 17-3 win over the Green Wave. Saturday, the Blue Devils outscored the Illini 17-3 over the final 35 minutes of the game for a 31-27 win. After rushing for 227 yards against Tulane, Nate Sheppard had 147 yards and a TD against Illinois while also adding 41 receiving yards and two TD catches.

No. 23 Missouri: The Tigers scored their first win at Kansas since 2001 with a 38-21 win over the Jayhawks on Friday night. Kansas got the game a ton of attention during the week with its video that invoked the Civil War roots of the rivalry . And, according to Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz, it led to his decision for Missouri to throw for a TD with less than a minute to go while leading by 17. The 2025 iteration of the game was the first time Missouri and Kansas had played each other since the Tigers left the Big 12. And they're not scheduled to meet again until 2031.

South Florida: USF is now 2-0 under new coach Brian Hartline after a 28-24 win at Army in an early American Conference matchup. Former LSU QB Michael Van Buren accounted for all four of USF's touchdowns and scored twice in the final four minutes as the Bulls overcame a 10-point deficit. Van Buren scored on a 24-yard run with 3:13 to go to cut Army's lead to three before leading USF on a 10-play, 81-yard drive that culminated in a 38-yard TD pass on fourth down to Joshua Porter with 19 seconds to go.

No. 15 BYU: The Cougars are off to a great start in their quest to get back to the Big 12 title game. BYU beat Arizona 28-17 in a game that could prove pivotal at the top of the Big 12 at the end of the season. Bear Bachmeier was 16-of-26 passing for 217 yards and three scores and rushed for BYU's other touchdown. Bachmeier scored once in each quarter as the Cougars blanked the Wildcats in the second half.

Pitt: A week after QB Mason Heintschel tied a school record with seven TD passes, the Panthers leaned on a strong defensive effort for a 12-7 home win over UCF. The Knights had just 206 total yards — and 20 rushing yards on 22 carries — and didn't score until the fourth quarter. Pitt went scoreless in the second half, but the 12 points the Panthers had in the first half were more than enough. A short week against Syracuse looms on Thursday night, but a Saturday night trip to Virginia Tech on Oct. 2 is suddenly very intriguing in the ACC.

Boise State: At the moment, Boise State's loss to Oregon doesn't look as good as it did immediately after the fact. But the Broncos rebounded with a 38-20 win over Memphis on Saturday. After the Tigers led 20-17 at half, Boise State scored 21 straight in the second half as Dylan Riley rushed for 206 yards on 19 carries. QB Maddux Madsen threw for a TD and rushed for another as the win could be a key data point for Boise State in the group of six playoff conversation.

No. 1 Ohio State's clock management : With a defense that had given up 15 and 13-play drives on Texas' last two possessions during a hot night in Austin, why didn't the Buckeyes let Texas go ahead earlier?

After Texas got to the Ohio State 1 yard-line with less than 90 seconds to go, the Longhorns didn't score until there were 25 seconds on the clock. Yes, it took Texas three plays, but the odds of Ohio State getting four stops in that situation were very slim. Ryan Day should have let Texas score with over a minute to go and a timeout in his back pocket.

Rutgers: We have to include the Scarlet Knights in this category for another week after a 28-21 loss to Boston College on Friday night. Rutgers has few contenders for the status of worst power conference team in the country at the moment and is staring 0-3 in the face. No. 14 USC visits Piscataway in Week 3. And while FCS opponent Howard may provide a brief respite in Week 4, that game is followed by a home game against No. 5 Indiana in Week 5.

Minnesota: The Gophers had no shot against Mississippi State on Saturday. The Bulldogs scored 14 points in each of the first two quarters as Kamario Taylor picked apart the Minnesota secondary. Taylor finished the game 16-of-22 passing for 227 yards and three touchdowns while a run game that has sustained the Minnesota offense in PJ Fleck's time in charge was absolutely nonexistent. Even when accounting for the 12 yards lost on sacks of Drake Lindsey, Minnesota rushed 13 times for 25 yards.

Liberty: It's been a swift fall for a team that was in the Fiesta Bowl after an undefeated season in 2023. Liberty got its first win since Nov. 1, 2025, on Saturday. But it wasn't an easy one. It should have been. The Flames beat FCS Gardner-Webb 24-23 thanks to a 54-yard TD with 2:34 to go. Liberty entered the game as a 25.5-point favorite as the most well-financed program in Conference USA.

Purdue: The Boilermakers are still searching for their first win over a power conference team since 2023. And they came oh-so-close on Saturday. Wake Forest eked out a 38-36 win in double overtime as Gio Lopez tied the game with a 3-yard run and then converted the game-winning 2-point conversion. Purdue scored 10 points in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter and had a great chance for a game-winning TD. But the Boilermakers had to settle for a 20-yard field goal as time expired for the tie.

UNLV: So much for the Rebels' status as a College Football Playoff sleeper as the Group of Six representative in the field. After losing to Memphis in Week Zero, the Rebels fell to 1-2 with a 44-6 loss at an overhauled North Texas squad. UNLV fumbled three times as part of four turnovers and had just 301 yards on 72 plays

articles.title: Lane Kiffin, LSU vs. LA Tech Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers rebounded from a slow start to pick up a 45-14 win over the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers rebounded from a slow start to pick up a 45-14 win over the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.

LSU was only ahead by three points at halftime and quarterback Sam Leavitt threw three interceptions, but the Tigers found another level in the second half to pull away from their in-state foe.

LSU thought it was on the way to cruising to a win in the first quarter, when it went up 10-0.

Leavitt produced the first of his career high three rushing touchdowns to extend the advantage to 10 points.

However, the Tigers experienced a world of struggles in the second quarter.

Leavitt threw three interceptions, including one that was returned 100 yards for a touchdown.

All of the struggles seemed to be washed away once the second half began.

LSU put up 28 unanswered points. Leavitt ran in for two more scores and fed Trey'Dez Green on a 10-yard touchdown pass.

The big positive for LSU is that it found a way to rebound in the second half and win by 31 points, but things have to be much cleaner ahead of its much-anticipated SEC opener in Week 3.

Kiffin makes his return to Oxford to play the Ole Miss Rebels in primetime next Saturday.

articles.title: Arch Manning, Sayin, Jeremiah Smith Box Score Stats, Highlights, Heisman Hype from Ohio State-Texas
articles.summary: Arch Manning led the Texas Longhorns on one of the best comebacks in recent college football memory to beat Julian Sayin, Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes.
articles.body:
Arch Manning led the Texas Longhorns on one of the best comebacks in recent college football memory to beat Julian Sayin, Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes.

Manning and the Longhorns scored 21 fourth-quarter points to erase a 17-point deficit and knock off the top-ranked team in the country.

Manning recovered from a brutal opening half to lead the fourth-ranked Longhorns to a victory.

The Texas quarterback hit Ryan Wingo on a touchdown pass to begin the comeback.

Manning played well on the two other scoring drives in the fourth quarter, both of which resulted in rushing touchdowns by Hollywood Smothers.

Smothers ran in the game-winning touchdown with 25 seconds left.

Prior to the Texas comeback, Sayin, Smith and Ohio State broke out to a sizable advantage.

Smith looked unstoppable through stretches of the first half. He was the game's leading receiver with 164 yards and a score.

Smith's production dried up, and in turn, so did the Buckeyes' scoring potential.

Sayin threw for 278 yards, one touchdown and an interception. He played well, but he was ultimately overshadowed by Manning's come-from-behind effort.

Texas' win now sets it up for a chance to be No. 1 in the AP poll on Monday. The Longhorns are next in action in Week 3 against UTSA. Ohio State returns home to face Kent State.

articles.title: Everything Lane Kiffin Said About LSU's Slow Start in Win vs. Louisiana Tech
articles.summary: LSU coach Lane Kiffin wasn't happy with his team's slow start to a Saturday matchup against Louisiana Tech.
articles.body:
LSU coach Lane Kiffin wasn't happy with his team's slow start to a Saturday matchup against Louisiana Tech.

The Tigers went into halftime with just a three-point lead over the Bulldogs before pulling away in the final two quarters of a 45-14 win.

"Turn the ball over four times in the game... really disappointing, there," Kiffin told reporters after Saturday's win. "Credit to LA Tech. Those guys did a really good job defensively, of playing really hard."

Kiffin continued, "We've got to execute better. Sam's got to do a better job of taking care of the ball."

LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt led the Tigers on a field goal and touchdown drive in the first quarter before losing control of a disastrous second.

Wide receiver Tre Wilson III lost a fumble on the first offensive drive of the quarter. Leavitt ended LSU's next three possessions with a trio of interceptions, one of which was returned for a 100-yard pick six.

"It's hard, because he's very competitive," Kiffin said about Leavitt. "You can see that, in some plays, trying too much there because we're not doing well."

When asked what his message to the locker room would be at halftime, Kiffin said, "Taking care of the ball on offense."

LSU outscored the visitors 35-7 in the second quarter to close out the victory. Leavitt finished the game having gone 25-for-38 with 344 passing yards and four total touchdowns to go along with the three interceptions.

"Maybe it was perfect for us, that we needed something like that, because if we played good on offense, and the game was 70-7 or something, then we don't have their attention," Kiffin said. "So, maybe it's what we needed. And we're in a good place.

"We're winning by 31 points and we're really upset. We've got a good standard going... second half was 35-7. That's a lot of people doing things right."

LSU has just one week to bounce back from Saturday's shaky start before one of the biggest matchups of the season.

The Tigers are slated to face Ole Miss, Kiffin's former program and their first SEC opponent of the season, on the road next Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ryan Day Discusses Ohio State Not Letting Texas Score Intentionally, Blowing 20-Point Lead in Loss
articles.summary: Ohio State coach Ryan Day says he considered intentionally allowing a Texas touchdown late in Saturday's 24-23 loss to the Longhorns.
articles.body:
Ohio State coach Ryan Day says he considered intentionally allowing a Texas touchdown late in Saturday's 24-23 loss to the Longhorns.

Texas was trailing by six points when the Longhorns got the ball to the one-yard line with 1:20 remaining.

The Buckeyes offense got the ball back with less than 30 seconds remaining after playing out the drive, a decision Day said he made after Ohio State's defense blocked Texas on second down.

"We talked about it, and decided that we were gonna play defense on second down," Day told reporters after the loss. "And then when we got that stop, right there, we said, 'Alright, we're gonna take our chances. Put the ball down for one yard and see if we can stop them for two downs and win the game.'

"If they were to score there, on second down, then we would have gone from there... it didn't work out."

The Buckeyes held a 23-3 lead heading into Saturday's fourth quarter before Texas completed a historic comeback.

Ohio State had not lost a game in which the team led by at least 20 points since 2011, per CBS Sports' Brandon Marcello .

Texas' comeback started when Arch Manning began the fourth quarter by marching his team 91 yards down the field on a 15-play touchdown drive before the Buckeyes went three-and-out on their next possession.

Ohio State's defense once again struggled to contain the Longhorn's run game, which was powered by running back Hollywood Smothers, as Texas completed a second straight scoring drive to get within six points.

"When it was time to get pressure, when we needed to, we weren't able to do that at a high enough rate, and especially when the game was on the line. That's the bottom line," Day said.

The Buckeyes got within range of a field goal on the next possession but missed from 45 yards out to set the Longhorns up for a potential winning drive.

"We really played well for three quarters and then didn't play well enough in the fourth quarter... We know that's the biggest part of the season," Day said. "We have to win the fourth quarter, especially on the road."

Day continued, "When you look at not being able to get off the field on defense, when you're really not able to sustain any drives on offense, and then we missed the field goal— all three phases didn't get it done in the fourth quarter, so we've all got to own that."

Ohio State will look to bounce back from Texas' stunning comeback next Saturday when the Buckeyes resume play at noon against visiting Kent State.

articles.title: Missouri State retires Dennis Heim's No. 71: 'It blows my mind'
articles.summary: Missouri State football retired Dennis Heim's No. 71 during halftime of Saturday's game. What he had to say about the celebration.
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD — Hundreds of people walked around Plaster Stadium wearing Monett No. 71 jerseys.

On the back of the jersey, Dennis Heim's name was printed.

Instead of a shirt, Heim's name will forever be enshrined inside Missouri State's football stadium. Heim, a Monett native, became the fifth person to have a jersey retired in Bears history.

During halftime of Missouri State's 48-14 win over Lindenwood, Heim stood with his loved ones at midfield on Saturday, Sept. 12.

Missouri State athletic director Patrick Randell spoke to the crowd about Heim's impact. The former Missouri State player was able to speak to the crowd, too. Heim was honored with a rousing applause from the 12,000 people in attendance.

"It blows my mind, honestly," Heim said. "This is a really big deal, but the outpouring of positive vibes and love from all of these people, it's overwhelming. I'm just so grateful."

See our best photos from Missouri State football vs Lindenwood in Week 2

Heim was a standout player for Missouri State from 1974-77. He still holds the all-time sack record with 41. During his junior season, Heim recorded 16 sacks, which is also a school record.

While he enjoys having the record, Heim wants someone from this modern-day crop of players to take it away from him.

"I've been hoping for a long time that it would," Heim said. "After I graduated, I had no idea that I had the sack record. Back in the 70s, that stuff just wasn't out there as much. At the time, I went out there to play as hard as I could."

After Missouri State's big win, head coach Casey Woods spoke at length about Heim's impact on the university. In Woods' short time in Springfield, he understands how necessary it was to honor a Bear great with this ceremony. 2

"Dennis Heim is an unbelievable ambassador for this place," Woods said. "He is someone that genuinely loves Missouri State. He would go fight for this place. There are not a lot of guys like No. 71."

Missouri State football vs Lindenwood: Bears win first game

Heim is excited for Missouri State's future, he said. He can feel Missouri State football's rise and the momentum behind the program. In the two years at the FBS level, Missouri State has been moving in the right direction.

It's a direction that makes him proud to be a Bear. As Missouri State continues to make history, Heim's number will always be revered in Plaster Stadium.

"For the longest time, I feel like football, perhaps, neglected for a little bit," Heim said. "I'm just ecstatic to see that football has the opportunity to contribute to the rest of the athletic department. As we know, rising tides lift all ships."

Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. Send stats or information to him at Lkeating@usatodayco.com

articles.title: El estado de gracia de Güler aviva el debate
articles.standfirst: El turco revolucionó al Bernabéu en 23 minutos ante el Rayo, con una exhibición que reabre la pregunta por su suplencia y confirma que atraviesa su mejor momento de blanco
articles.summary: El turco revolucionó al Bernabéu en 23 minutos ante el Rayo, con una exhibición que reabre la pregunta por su suplencia y confirma que atraviesa su mejor momento de blanco
articles.body: Explicar el partido de Arda Güler ante el Rayo es narrar la cronología de un escándalo. Fueron apenas 23 minutos sobre el césped, pero qué 23 minutos. Su irrupción fue, con diferencia, la nota más brillante de una noche en la que el Madrid volvió a golear pese a mostrar dos caras distintas, lastrado por el físico en una semana que le depara dos compromisos exigentes antes del parón, con la visita al Metropolitano como plato fuerte. Güler entró en el minuto 72 para agitar un partido que se le estaba haciendo bola al Madrid. El Rayo había hilvanado varias llegadas de peligro que volvieron a sacar a relucir la mejor versión de Courtois, con paradas de mérito e incluso un disparo al palo. En ese contexto de zozobra, el turco apareció para poner orden y algo de equilibrio. Dio control al juego, se dejó ver por todas las zonas y se erigió en un torbellino desatado en tareas ofensivas. Lo primero que hizo fue repartir dos balones que fueron auténticos caramelos. Uno de ellos, a la cabeza de Dumfries, que de no mediar una gran parada de Audero habría supuesto el primer gol del neerlandés de blanco. Después estuvo cerca de provocar un penalti y, acto seguido, probó al meta rayista desde fuera del área con otro disparo envenenado. Puro descaro en cada intervención. Sus minutos entre líneas fueron una delicia para el paladar de los más exquisitos del Bernabéu. Combinó con un Bellingham al que se le agotaba la gasolina, con Mbappé y con Vinicius, tejiendo el juego con una sencillez al alcance de muy pocos. Y fue precisamente al galo a quien asistió en el 4-1 que cerró la goleada, la rúbrica perfecta a un cuarto de hora de ensueño. Ante semejante exhibición, muchos se preguntaron por su suplencia, más aún viniendo de estar sancionado y no haber jugado entre semana ante el Inter. La explicación, sin embargo, tenía nombre propio: Mourinho reservó la titularidad para dar la primera oportunidad en esa posición a Diomande, el fichaje más caro de la historia del club, un estreno que se estaba haciendo esperar. De ahí la disyuntiva. El propio técnico salió al paso en rueda de prensa, consciente del runrún. "Arda juega mucho, pero estoy cien por cien seguro de que si hoy no juega Diomande de titular, la primera pregunta sería por qué no juega o cuándo juega", razonó. "En nuestro banquillo solo se ve calidad, y las preguntas van a ser cada partido por qué juega uno y no el otro. Arda es muy bueno. Brahim hizo un gran partido ante el Inter. Diomande está trabajando para mejorar y tiene un gran potencial". El debate, en cualquier caso, vuelve a estar más vivo que nunca, porque Güler se ha convertido en imprescindible por todo lo que genera para los suyos. Es un futbolista diferente, atraviesa su mejor momento desde que aterrizó en Madrid y quizá sea, junto a Bernardo Silva, el que más fútbol atesora hoy en la plantilla. Prescindir del turco, a estas alturas, se antoja casi un pecado. En el horizonte asoman Elche y el Metropolitano, este último el primer gran examen del curso para los de Mou. La temporada pasada, casi por estas fechas, el Madrid de Xabi Alonso cayó goleado en el feudo colchonero. Aquella tarde, eso sí, Güler dejó su huella pese a la derrota, un aviso de que en las grandes citas el turco siempre quiere ser protagonista.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 2
articles.summary: After a chalky Week 1 of the 2026 season, college football fans were quickly reminded that chaos reigns supreme with an upset-laden Week 2 slate.
articles.body:
After a chalky Week 1 of the 2026 season, college football fans were quickly reminded that chaos reigns supreme with an upset-laden Week 2 slate.

Michigan followed up its controversial Week 1 victory over Western Michigan with an upset of Oklahoma, while Oregon fell to an Oklahoma State team that just lost to Tulsa to open the season, handing a pair of presumptive College Football Playoff contenders an early loss.

The game of the week also lived up to the hype, as Texas rallied from down 23-3 to beat Ohio State and make a compelling case to be considered the nation's top team at this early juncture.

Now it's time for Bleacher Report's updated top 25 ranking, with the college football writing staff of David Kenyon, Adam Kramer, Joel Reuter and Brad Shepard making up our voting panel.

Note: These rankings will be updated to reflect the Utah vs. Arkansas and USC vs. Louisiana results, if needed.

25. Mississippi State (2-0, Previous Rank: NR)

Week 2 Result: WIN at Minnesota (38-13) Next Week: at South Carolina

The Bulldogs got an early road test under their belt against Minnesota in Week 2, and the defense shined, limiting Drake Lindsey to 5.8 yards per attempt on 48 passes and the Golden Gophers' collective rushing attack to 13 yards on 15 carries. Quarterback Kamario Taylor had 227 passing yards, 86 rushing yards and three touchdowns, a week after he had 413 total yards and five scores in a blowout win against UL Monroe.

24. Virginia Tech (2-0, Previous Rank: NR)

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Old Dominion (44-21) Next Week: at Maryland

After hanging 73 points on VMI in their opener, the Virginia Tech offense was humming again on Saturday. The Hokies built a 34-6 halftime lead, and quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer had a 327-yard, two-touchdown day through the air to lead the offensive attack. The running game only managed 89 yards and 2.1 yards per carry, which led to Grunkemeyer attempting 41 passes, so they will need to find more balance in ACC play.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Oklahoma (17-10) Next Week: vs. UTEP

After a noisy week amid blowback from their controversial win against Western Michigan and reaction to comments from head coach Kyle Whittingham on Bryce Underwood's potentially tenuous hold on the starting quarterback job, the Wolverines scored a signature win at the Big House on Saturday. They took a 10-0 lead into halftime and the defense dug in down the stretch, limiting the Sooners to an interception, a punt, a turnover on downs and a stalled final drive as time expired.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Iowa State (16-13) Next Week: vs. Northern Iowa

It wasn't pretty, but it rarely is in the grind-it-out Cy-Hawk rivalry, and the Hawkeyes came out on top thanks to a 42-yard field goal from kicker Caden Buhr with 15 seconds remaining to break a 13-13 tie. Both teams scored a touchdown in the second quarter on successive possessions, and then it was simply a game of defense, field position and kicking. Freshman Tony Diaz (8 catches, 95 yards) continues to provide a spark offensively, while Hank Brown was 21-of-30 for 191 yards while also adding a rushing score.

Week 2 Result: LOSS at Michigan (10-17) Next Week: vs. New Mexico

Michigan punted in a 10-10 game with 9:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, but Sooners quarterback John Mateer threw an interception on the subsequent drive and the Wolverines responded with a touchdown. The Sooners then ran 13 plays across three separate drives the rest of the way and managed just 25 total yards, resulting in a punt, a turnover on downs and the clock running out. Mateer finished with 189 passing yards, 45 rushing yards and one touchdown, as his dual-threat impact was significantly limited.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Villanova (59-13) Next Week: vs. SMU

After perhaps the best performance in a loss of any team in Week 1 when they fell 41-38 in a nail-biter against Ole Miss, Louisville took its turn at a cupcake game on Friday night in a blowout win over Villanova. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz had 332 passing yards, 42 rushing yards and four total touchdowns, leading the charge for a Cardinals offensive attack that piled up 635 total yards and found the end zone twice in each quarter.

Week 2 Result: WIN at Kansas (38-21) Next Week: vs. Troy

The Border War rivalry game returned after a 13-year hiatus in 2025 with a 42-31 Missouri victory, and the Tigers came out on top again on Friday night, though it was a 14-14 tie at halftime. Linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. swung the momentum coming out of halftime with a fumble recovery and an interception on the first two Kansas drives of the third quarter as Mizzou turned both of those takeaways into touchdowns. Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons (19-of-29, 292 yards, 3 TD) had another strong game under center.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Southern (77-6) Next Week: at Texas Tech

The Cougars scored a touchdown on each of their first 11 offensive possessions and piled up a whopping 388 rushing yards and six rushing scores for one of the most lopsided victories on the Week 2 slate. It was a well-timed blowout following a less-than-convincing showing against Oregon State last weekend, and should provide some welcome momentum heading into a big Week 3 showdown with Texas Tech. Defensively, holding the opposition to negative-six rushing yards on 22 carries deserves a mention, regardless of the opposition.

Week 2 Result: WIN at Temple (27-9) Next Week: vs. Buffalo

The Nittany Lions were 23.5-point favorites against Temple in a neutral-site game at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, but found themselves in a close game early when they posted a missed field goal, punt and turnover on downs before finally putting points on the board with 6:51 remaining in the first half. That was the start of 27 unanswered points en route to a comfortable win, but the early struggles moving the ball were troubling nonetheless. Rocco Becht finished 21-of-27 for 268 yards and three touchdowns after a four-touchdown performance in their opener.

Week 2 Result: Leading 29-3 at halftime vs. Arkansas Next Week: vs. Utah State

Full analysis will be added after the conclusion of the game.

Week 2 Result: WIN at Georgia Tech (45-24) Next Week: vs. Kennesaw State

True freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon (10-of-21, 148 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) didn't have the most efficient game under center, but he protected the football, and DeSean Bishop (20 carries, 147 yards, 2 TD) led the way for a rushing attack that pounded out 45 carries for 299 yards. The Volunteers scored 24 unanswered points across the second and third quarters to seize control and score a road win against a Power Four opponent.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. UC Davis (56-10) Next Week: at Louisville

After a bizarre season opener where a power surge delayed kickoff by nearly two hours and the Mustangs escaped with a 27-24 victory over Florida State, it was a far more comfortable Week 2 performance against an outgunned UC Davis squad. Kevin Jennings threw for 337 yards and five touchdowns, and backup Ty Hawkins added two more scores en route to a staggering 454 passing yards on only 32 attempts as a team. A big early ACC showdown on the road against Louisville awaits next Saturday.

Week 2 Result: WIN at Oregon State (35-24) Next Week: vs. Houston

The Red Raiders trailed 24-21 early in the fourth quarter in a game where their defense was torched for 403 passing yards, but they clamped down when it mattered to force a punt and two turnovers on downs to pull away down the stretch. A 32-yard touchdown pass from Will Hammond to Coy Eakin with 6:37 remaining gave Texas Tech the lead for good, and the Red Raiders survived a scare from an Oregon State squad that also played Houston tough in Week 1.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Arizona (28-17) Next Week: at Colorado State

Bear Bachmeier (16-of-26, 217 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT) outplayed Noah Fifita (23-of-31, 230 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT) in a matchup of returning Big 12 starters. The BYU defense forced a decisive turnover on downs with 8:24 remaining in a 21-17 game, then the offense put things out of reach with an efficient four-play, 82-yard touchdown drive. The Cougars now have a relatively clear path to a 5-0 start before their Oct. 17 showdown with Notre Dame.

Week 2 Result: WIN at Kentucky (45-17) Next Week: vs. Florida State

Keelon Russell threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in an ugly game for both sides that featured six turnovers and 16 penalties, but the end result was still a 28-point conference win on the road for the Crimson Tide. A 17-16 Kentucky lead with 5:42 left in the third quarter devolved into a blowout when Alabama finally found another gear and strung together four consecutive touchdown drives. Daniel Hill was the offensive headliner, logging 18 carries for 104 yards and a touchdown.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Louisiana Tech (45-14) Next Week: at Ole Miss

No matter how you spin it, a three-interception game from Sam Leavitt against Louisiana Tech is not an ideal springboard for LSU heading into the SEC gauntlet with Ole Miss on the horizon next weekend. Sure, he also had 344 passing yards, a passing touchdown and three rushing touchdowns, but the margin for error is about to shrink by an astronomical margin. Credit the LSU defense for coming up with three takeaways of their own and allowing just 140 yards, but this game raised more red flags than green.

Week 2 Result: Leading 28-10 at halftime vs. Louisiana Next Week: at Rutgers

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Charlotte (41-9) Next Week: vs. LSU

After throwing 15 incompletions and a pick against Louisville in Week 1, Heisman Trophy candidate Trinidad Chambliss was nearly perfect against the Charlotte defense, completing 23-of-26 attempts for 225 yards and two touchdowns. Also encouraging, star running back Kewan Lacy had 13 carries for 87 yards and two touchdowns after a leg injury knocked him out of the Louisville game. The defense bent, allowing 322 yards, but ultimately surrendered just three field goals.

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Arizona State (48-20) Next Week: vs. Kentucky

The Aggies led just 24-20 heading into the fourth quarter, but scored 24 unanswered points, including a pair of Cutter Boley interceptions returned for touchdowns. The defense tallied four total takeaways on the day, helping to prop up a lackluster offense that managed just 255 total yards and 2.6 yards per carry on the ground. Marcel Reed finished 15-of-25 for 163 yards with three touchdowns and an interception, finding Isaiah Horton on two of his touchdown strikes.

Week 2 Result: LOSS at Texas (23-24) Next Week: vs. Kent State

The Buckeyes were in complete control for three quarters on Saturday night, carrying a 23-3 lead into the fourth quarter, but the offense had already started to stall after halftime, and the defense was unable to slow down the Texas attack on three consecutive long touchdown drives. Star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (8 catches, 164 yards, 1 TD) had another huge game, but the rest of the Ohio State offense was largely held in check, including a running game that finished with 31 carries for 94 yards.

5. Indiana Hoosiers (2-0, Previous Rank: 6)

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Howard (55-0) Next Week: vs. Western Kentucky

Josh Hoover threw four touchdown passes on only 11 pass attempts before heading to the sidelines, and the Hoosiers built a 41-0 lead heading into halftime against FCS opponent Howard.

While the passing game shined early, the running game also piled up 301 yards on 46 carries, while the defense allowed 57 yards on 47 plays from the Howard offense.

Through two games, the defending champs have outscored the opposition 107-17, including 65-6 in the first half. Expect another lopsided result next week against a Western Kentucky team that lost 70-20 to Georgia on Saturday.

4. Georgia Bulldogs (2-0, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Western Kentucky (70-20) Next Week: at Arkansas

It was another abbreviated game for Gunner Stockton and many of the Georgia starters, as the Bulldogs scored touchdowns on each of their first seven drives to build a 49-0 lead with 5:51 remaining in the second quarter.

Stockton finished 13-of-16 passing for 234 yards and five touchdowns, while the running game tallied 234 yards and an impressive 6.7 yards per carry. Backup quarterback Ryan Puglisi helped pad that total with a 70-yard touchdown run.

Both touchdowns from the Hilltoppers came in the fourth quarter facing largely reserves, as it was a 63-6 game before their first trip into the end zone.

3. Miami Hurricanes (2-0, Previous Rank: 3)

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Florida A&M (77-7) Next Week: at Wake Forest

The Hurricanes hung a school record 856 total yards of offense on a hapless Florida A&M defense, finding the end zone on 11 of their first 12 possessions, with the only exception being a kneel down before halftime in what was already a 49-0 blowout.

Darian Mensah (14-of-15, 252 yards, 3 TD), Mark Fletcher Jr. (7 carries, 105 yards, 2 TD) and Malachi Toney (4 catches, 96 yards, 1 TD) all got their work in before an early move to the sidelines, while backup quarterback Luke Nickel also completed all eight of his pass attempts for 144 yards and three touchdowns.

The defense allowed 2.3 yards per play, four first downs and 107 total yards, and the Rattlers' only points came on a 72-yard fumble return touchdown midway through the fourth quarter.

2. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (2-0, Previous Rank: 2)

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Rice (52-0) Next Week: vs. Michigan State

The Notre Dame defense allowed 128 total yards and a grand total of seven first downs while coming up with four takeaways in a smothering performance against a Rice team that has not had a winning season in more than a decade.

CJ Carr completed 16-of-20 pass attempts for 253 yards and four touchdowns before taking a seat on the sidelines, and even in a blowout, the Fighting Irish finished with more pass attempts (33) than rush attempts (32) as life after Jeremiyah Love brings a more balanced attack.

It was Notre Dame's first shutout since Nov. 19, 2022, when they blanked a Boston College team that finished 3-9.

1. Texas Longhorns (2-0, Previous Rank: 5)

Week 2 Result: WIN vs. Ohio State (24-23) Next Week: vs. UTSA

Down 23-3 entering the fourth quarter, the Longhorns came from behind with three methodical touchdown drives of 15 plays and 91 yards, 13 plays and 72 yards and 12 plays and 73 yards to avenge a 14-7 loss in the season opener a year ago.

The high-powered Ohio State offense was limited to three punts, a made field goal and a missed field goal after halftime, and that defensive effort paved the way for the unlikely comeback. Arch Manning finished 23-of-37 for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception, while Hollywood Smothers tallied 21 carries for 74 yards and two touchdowns, including the game-winning score.

The road ahead is a grind, but with the toughest opponent off the board in a thrilling victory, the Longhorns belong squarely in the national championship conversation.
